Check That Functions Exist in Installed Packages

Source: R/is_function_here.R
is_function_here.Rd

Checks that the required functions are present in the installed packages (e.g., not removed or renamed in another version of the package).

Usage

is_function_here(fun, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")

Arguments

fun

Vector of character strings: the required functions, each preceded by its package and "::" or ":::", without final "()" (e.g., c("stats::median", "grid::gpar")). "pkg::fun" requires an object exported by the package, "pkg:::fun" accepts any object of the package namespace (internal functions included). The object can be of any kind (e.g., "base::pi"), except lazy-loaded datasets (e.g., "datasets::iris"), which are not found. Operators and other non-syntactic names can be written with or without backticks (e.g., "base::+"), except the names starting with ":" (e.g., :=, ::), which must be written with backticks (e.g., "rlang::`:=`").

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

Invisible NULL if all the functions are present, otherwise an error. The namespaces of the checked packages are loaded (not attached).

See also

is_package_here, exists, getNamespaceExports.

Author

Gael Millot

Haiding Wang

Yushi Han

Examples

# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/is_function_here.html
saferDev::is_function_here(fun = base::c("stats::median", "grid::gpar"), safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
# Missing function: error
base::try(expr = saferDev::is_function_here(fun = "stats::notgood", safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = " INSIDE P1::F1"), silent = FALSE,
    outFile = base::getOption(x = "try.outFile", default = base::stderr()))
#> Error : 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR IN saferDev::is_function_here() INSIDE P1::F1
#> 
#> REQUIRED FUNCTION IS MISSING IN THE INSTALLED PACKAGE:
#> stats::notgood
#> 
#> IN ONE OF THESE FOLDERS:
#> /__w/_temp/Library
#> /usr/local/lib/R/site-library
#> /usr/local/lib/R/library
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> 
# Internal function (not exported): error with "::", no error with ":::"
base::try(expr = saferDev::is_function_here(fun = "stats::Pillai", safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = ""), silent = FALSE,
    outFile = base::getOption(x = "try.outFile", default = base::stderr()))
#> Error : 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR IN saferDev::is_function_here().
#> 
#> REQUIRED FUNCTION IS NOT EXPORTED BY THE INSTALLED PACKAGE:
#> stats::Pillai
#> 
#> WRITE ":::" INSTEAD OF "::" TO CHECK A NON EXPORTED FUNCTION.
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> 
saferDev::is_function_here(fun = "stats:::Pillai", safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = "")
# Package not written: error
base::try(expr = saferDev::is_function_here(fun = "c", safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""), silent = FALSE,
    outFile = base::getOption(x = "try.outFile", default = base::stderr()))
#> Error : 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR IN saferDev::is_function_here().
#> 
#> THE STRING IN fun ARGUMENT MUST BE WRITTEN "package::function" OR "package:::function":
#> c
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#>
